items.text: The minimum age to buy, possess and use cannabis in the Northwest Territories is 19, the same as the drinking age. Adults may carry up to 30 g of dried cannabis (or equivalent) in public. Legal cannabis is sold online by the NWT Liquor and Cannabis Commission (NTLCC) or in some NWT liquor stores.

Use is limited to private property where tobacco smoking is allowed, trails and roadways (when not driving), and parks not in use for a public event. Smoking or vaping cannabis is banned in places children frequent, such as playgrounds, school grounds, sports fields and outdoor events. In a vehicle, cannabis must be unopened or stored out of reach of the driver and passengers.
Community governments can make bylaws that add to the territory's rules on public use, and a community without a cannabis store can restrict or ban cannabis by plebiscite (a community vote).

Drinking in a public place isn't allowed unless specifically authorised. Residences, licensed premises and remote places used for outdoor recreation don't count as public places; public intoxication is always an offence. Each community can choose by plebiscite an unrestricted, restricted, committee-run or prohibited liquor system, set in its own regulations, so check the community's rules before bringing alcohol.
